subject: community-medicine
title: ICDS and the Anganwadi: Six Services, Growth Monitoring and Poshan

steps.title: ICDS: the world's largest childcare web
steps.tx: **Integrated Child Development Services** (1975) delivers early childhood care through Anganwadi centres covering roughly 400 to 800 population in plains norms (300 to 800 in difficult areas in revised patterns), targeting children under six, pregnant and lactating mothers and adolescent girls. It sits in women and child development, not the health ministry, the administrative fact behind every convergence question.
steps.say: Since 1975, one centre per few hundred people, run by women and child development, not health. Children under six, mothers and adolescent girls enter its register. Convergence questions start from that ministry split.

steps.title: Six services in one courtyard
steps.tx: The **six ICDS services** are supplementary nutrition, immunisation (with health department), health check-ups, referral services, nutrition and health education, and non-formal preschool education. Only nutrition and preschool education are the Anganwadi worker's own delivery; the rest arrive through convergence with the health system on VHSND and clinic days.
steps.say: Six services, two truly hers. Food and preschool education she delivers; immunisation, check-ups and referral arrive through health convergence. Stems test which services are direct and which are shared.

rows: Health system at centre or VHSND

steps.title: Supplementary nutrition norms
steps.tx: **Supplementary feeding** provides about 500 kilocalories and 12 to 15 grams protein daily to children 6 months to 6 years for 300 days a year, and about 600 kilocalories with 18 to 20 grams protein to pregnant and lactating mothers, with double rations for severely underweight children in current norms (hot cooked meals or take-home rations by state model).
steps.say: Numbers feed children: five hundred calories and twelve to fifteen grams protein, three hundred days yearly; mothers six hundred. Severely underweight children draw double. Hot meals or take-home rations vary by state model.

steps.title: Growth monitoring: weighing with meaning
steps.tx: **Growth monitoring** weighs under-fives monthly (birth to 3 years most intensively), plotting weight-for-age on road-to-health charts with green, yellow and red zones under WHO standards. A flattening curve triggers counselling before the zone changes; growth faltering, not static low weight, is the actionable signal. ICDS registers historically ran to eleven-plus books per worker.
steps.say: Weigh, plot, act on flattening. Monthly weights on zoned charts; a flattening line triggers counselling before colour changes. Faltering direction beats static position as the action signal.

steps.title: Poshan Abhiyaan and the malnutrition mission
steps.tx: **Poshan Abhiyaan** (2018) layered a mission over ICDS: convergence across ministries, real-time growth monitoring technology, and annual targets (stunting reduction of 2 percent per year in its original arithmetic), with Poshan Maah and Pakhwada community mobilisations. Malnutrition's multisector causes (food, care, water, infection) are the mission's explicit logic model.
steps.say: A 2018 mission layered convergence over the old web. Technology-tracked growth, cross-ministry targets, community mobilisation months. Food, care, water and infection together form its stated logic model.

steps.title: Underweight, stunting, wasting: three failures
steps.tx: **Anthropometric failures** separate cleanly: underweight is low weight-for-age (composite), stunting low height-for-age (chronic), wasting low weight-for-height (acute). NFHS-5 put Indian under-five stunting near 35.5 percent, wasting near 19.3 and underweight near 32.1 in round teaching figures. Each index accuses a different time scale of deprivation.
steps.say: Three indices, three clocks. Weight-for-age composite, height-for-age chronic, weight-for-height acute. Indian figures sit near thirty five, nineteen and thirty two percent. Time scale decides which index accuses.

steps.title: Severe acute malnutrition pathway
steps.tx: **Severe acute malnutrition** (weight-for-height below minus 3 SD, mid-upper arm circumference under 11.5 cm, or nutritional oedema) with appetite and no complications manages at community level with medical nutrition therapy per protocol; complications or failed appetite go to nutrition rehabilitation centres for stabilised feeding phases. MUAC tapes put the diagnosis in mothers' hands in family-led screening models.
steps.say: Arm tapes diagnose in seconds. Under eleven point five centimetres, severe wasting or oedema enters protocol care; complications go to rehabilitation centres. Mothers themselves screen in family-led models.

steps.title: Anganwadi worker: training, registers, overload
steps.tx: The **Anganwadi worker** is a local woman with job and refresher training, maintaining registers from household survey to growth charts and stock, assisted by a helper for cooking and child handling. Workload expansion (surveys, digital entry, scheme enrolment drives) against honorarium status mirrors the ASHA tension and appears in the same examination essays.
steps.say: Local woman, expanding ledger. A dozen registers, digital entry, scheme drives, helper beside her, honorarium not salary. Her overload essay writes parallel to the ASHA one.

rows: Anganwadi helper for cooking and care

steps.title: Convergence in action: VHSND again
steps.tx: **Convergence** becomes physical on village health and nutrition days: her platform hosts ANM immunisation and antenatal care while she supplies beneficiary lists, nutrition demonstration and growth data. Joint microplans (health plus ICDS) with shared due lists are the measurable output. Where convergence fails, the same child is weighed hungry beside a vaccine she never receives.
steps.say: Convergence is a shared list, not a slogan. Her platform and lists, health's vaccines and clinics, one due list. Failure looks like a weighed hungry child beside an unreached vaccine.
